title: Embedded AI evaluators won’t be an easy solution, Hugging Face’s policy chief says
slides: Why won't embedded AI evaluators solve everything?
Hugging Face's policy chief raises concerns.
Built-in evaluators may share the same blind spots.
You can't outsource judgment to the model itself.
Audit your evaluator's assumptions before trusting it.
thread_text:
1. Who evaluates the evaluators?

Hugging Face's policy chief just raised a flag: built-in AI evaluators may share the same blind spots as the models they check. That's not a bug—it's a structural risk.

2. Same model, same blind spots

When the evaluator is embedded in the same system, it inherits the same training data and biases. It's like asking a student to grade their own exam—and expecting objectivity.

3. Judgment can't be outsourced

The core issue: you can't delegate critical judgment to the model itself. Evaluation requires external standards, not just pattern matching from the same source.

4. Audit before you trust

Before relying on any evaluator, map its assumptions. What does it optimize for? What does it ignore? The answers reveal exactly where it will fail you.

5. Test your evaluator this week

Pick one evaluator you use and list three assumptions it makes. Then check: do those match your actual priorities? If not, you've found your first gap to fix.
